story: As the golden light fades over Magnolia Loop on this mild November evening, Gary asks Hal to look over his golf cart modification form before filing it, with lights and a sound system planned for the parade. Donna, delighted, promises a dessert for Rosa's Friday dinner, and Rosa invites everyone to bring their best, including Donna's flamingo count that Hal is eager to tally. Hal, dutifully, sets out to count the pink flamingos visible from the street, notebook in hand.
events: Hal (donna flamingo flock): Count the flamingos visible from the street, one by one, and note the tally in my notebook

gary.thought_process: Donna already told me Tuesday is on, paddle packed and all, so I don't need to ask again. Rosa and Hal are handling the Friday dinner, and my cornbread's already promised. What I haven't done is move on the cart. Hal offered to check my Architectural Review form line by line, and the parade rig needs approval before I bolt anything visible to the cart (L-01). Hal's right here, so I can use this moment instead of standing around chatting.

parameters.content: Hal, got a minute to look over my cart modification form before I file it? Lights and a sound system for the parade, and I want it right the first time. I'll keep the speakers off after ten, you have my word.

donna.thought_process: Three people just talked at me at once, and nobody's had my answer yet. Rosa's dinner Friday is a yes, since I'm not about to miss a social event, and saying it also settles Hal's expectation. Gary wants pickleball before Friday, which feeds my doubles-partner goal. I'll answer Rosa first, accept warmly, and fold in a quick promise to Gary and Hal so I'm not repeating my earlier line about Tuesday. Flamingo count can happen tomorrow, fair and square.

parameters.content: Rosa, yes, put me down for Friday, and I'll bring a dessert so you don't have to lift a finger. Gary, Thursday morning for third-shot drops, and Hal, we'll count my flamingos right after, fair and square.

hal.thought_process: Rosa, Gary, and Donna are all gathered and I already made my offer to Donna last tick about counting her flamingos fair and square. She hasn't answered yet, and I shouldn't ask again. The flock is right here on Magnolia Loop, so the honest thing is to do the count myself, line by line, the way I'd inventory supplies. L-02 says three ornaments visible from the street. I'll tally what I can see and write it down so nobody can argue later. I'll report it fairly, and if the number's over, we'll talk about it neighbor to neighbor before any committee gets involved.

parameters.content: Count the flamingos visible from the street, one by one, and note the tally in my notebook

rosa.thought_process: I already invited Donna and she hasn't answered me directly yet. She and Gary are planning Tuesday pickleball, and Hal wants to count flamingos with her. All three neighbors are standing right here, and the dinner is Friday. I shouldn't ask again. Better to lock in the details so nobody can wiggle out: time, what to bring, and a nudge to Donna that her seat is set. Keep it short and warm, with a little bluntness.

parameters.content: Donna, dinner is Friday at six at my place, roast pork, and all you need to bring is yourself. Bring your flamingo count too, Hal's already sharpening his pencil.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
